nodes.claim: The perfect bank serves each person the question that maximizes expected information about them — under the constraint that comparison requires shared ground.
nodes.detail: Pure adaptive selection (ask whatever is most informative next) and pure uniformity (everyone answers everything) are both wrong: the first destroys cohort comparability, the second wastes the answer budget. The perfect axiom is the constrained optimum — a shared spine every person answers (comparability), with the remaining budget allocated adaptively (information). InSight's core/tail split is the practical shadow of exactly this theorem. 2026-08-27: the seed's open problem (the right spine size as a function of population and question count) is refined by que-5 — the size function gains the cross-axiom coupling portfolio as a third argument (entering through dimension coverage), and the spine's composition is set on the joint person-space rather than the bank's own, within que-5's stated boundary; que-6 grounds the spine's linking role in the equating literature. 'Information about them' therefore means information about the joint coordinates, not the bank-internal ones — central's 2026-08-26 question is answered at que-5.

nodes.claim: A question is a measurement instrument with estimable parameters — including which response-process family it obeys — and the perfect bank calibrates those parameters continuously from live answers.
nodes.detail: Raised conjecture→cited 2026-08-27; the seed's scout task is answered and the answer resharpened the claim in two places. (i) The instrument frame is canonical: an item carries parameters relative to latent traits — Birnbaum's two-parameter logistic for binary items, Samejima's graded response model for ordinal — and person and item parameters are recovered from response data. One correction to the seed's wording: the workhorse is Bock & Aitkin's MARGINAL maximum likelihood (item parameters estimated by integrating over the ability distribution), not literally joint estimation. (ii) The resharpening: 'difficulty/discrimination' presupposes a DOMINANCE process — endorsement rising monotonically with the trait — which is standard for ability items and contested for opinion and attitude items. Attitude statements often behave as unfolding items: a person disagrees both when the statement is too extreme and when it is too mild, so the response function is single-peaked (Roberts–Donoghue–Laughlin's generalized graded unfolding model; Stark et al. 2006 find ideal-point models fit personality items as well or better; Drasgow et al. 2010 argue Likert-style dominance scoring of such data has been misguided). One term disambiguated by this run's adversarial pass: 'ideal point' names two different model classes — the unfolding sense above (single-peaked response function) and the spatial-voting sense, in which the person carries an ideal point but the item response function is MONOTONE. Clinton–Jackman–Rivers' Bayesian roll-call model is the latter: its quadratic-utility spatial model reduces to a 2PL-equivalent monotone form, so it proves large-scale Bayesian estimation of binary opinion data while sitting on the dominance side, and is cited here as that contrast case, not as unfolding evidence. The perfect bank therefore holds the response-process family per item as an ESTIMABLE property, not an assumption — with the honest limit that the families are not always distinguishable from response data alone (Fu–Tan–Kyllonen 2026: an unfolding model can reproduce a dominance model's curves given an informative prior at, or fixing of, an extreme item location). (iii) 'Calibrates continuously' is a real literature, not a metaphor: online item calibration in operational adaptive testing (van der Linden & Ren's optimal Bayesian calibration design; Ren–van der Linden–Diao's continuous online calibration), with Stocking 1988 naming the standing failure mode — scale drift when live calibration optimizes against current estimates. (iv) InSight connection kept from the seed: the nightly fit's published loading vectors are item parameters in all but name; selection (que-1/que-5) should run on measured item profiles rather than topic labels — the first REQUESTS row asks for exactly that exposure. Verification note: this container's egress policy blocks publisher full-text; every source was corroborated at search-index/metadata level against the publisher's own indexed record plus at least one independent record (the body lane's 2026-08-27 precedent), and the full set was independently re-verified by this run's adversarial pass. nodes.claim: Question production is a closed loop: measured performance teaches the next question's shape.
nodes.detail: InSight already runs the shadow of this (the scorecard: evenness, leaders' shapes, vintage comparison). The perfect version closes the loop tighter: every authored question is a hypothesis about what will split people, its live performance is the experiment, and the generator learns shape-level rules (length, concreteness, tension type) from measured outcomes — with the standing guardrail that warmth outranks any score, because a bank optimized to maximal disagreement converges on outrage, which is a worse instrument for every other axiom's purposes. Grounding path queued 2026-08-27: the automatic item generation and item-quality-prediction literature is the scout direction that would raise this node.

nodes.claim: Portability across culture and language is established per question and cohort, never assumed — and comparison is graded to the level of invariance actually established, labeled with its basis.
nodes.detail: Raised conjecture→cited 2026-08-27, and the claim WEAKENED into its defensible form on the scout's evidence: the seed said 'refuses cross-cohort comparison where invariance fails', but the literature says the refusal must be graded, because exact invariance rarely holds across many groups and methods exist precisely to define what comparison remains legal beneath it. Grounding: the invariance taxonomy — configural through strict factorial — and why comparability precedes comparison (Meredith 1993; Davidov et al. 2014 is the umbrella review); partial invariance as the original definition of legal comparison under failure (Byrne–Shavelson–Muthén 1989); alignment and Bayesian approximate invariance as many-group methods that permit mean/variance comparison WITHOUT exact invariance (Asparouhov & Muthén 2014; van de Schoot et al. 2013); the construct/method/item-bias taxonomy separating translation and cultural context as distinct threat classes (van de Vijver & Tanzer 2004); and the empirical anchor that translation itself moves item functioning — differential item functioning grows with linguistic and cultural distance across TIMSS's 57 countries and 43 languages, with language-version differences more influential than country differences (Gökçe et al. 2021). Held honestly, the live controversy: Welzel et al. argue in print that detected non-invariance is often artifactual (closed-ended scale arithmetic under sample-mean disparity) and that invariance testing blocks substantively valid comparisons; Meuleman et al. answer in the same journal that the statistical argument is wrong; Funder & Gardiner argue conventional invariance benchmarks are strict enough to effectively prohibit cross-cultural research and urge external validity as the better criterion. The perfect axiom's rule is therefore not 'invariance or silence' but InSight's honesty grammar generalized: establish the level of comparability per question and cohort by a NAMED method (exact, partial, approximate, alignment), license only the comparisons that level supports, state the basis with the reading — and refuse outright only where even graded comparability cannot be established. Verification note: publisher full-text egress-blocked from this container; all sources corroborated at search-index/metadata level, each against at least two independent records, and independently re-verified by this run's adversarial pass.

nodes.claim: The combination bends the spine twice — composition toward identifying the joint person-space, size through the coupling portfolio's dimension-coverage floor; within-bank information alone selects the right spine only in the degenerate case where the joint space is a nonsingular reparameterization of the bank's own and no cross-instrument map remains to be estimated.
nodes.detail: Answers central's 2026-08-26 question directly: no, the optimal spine is not chosen for within-bank information alone — with the claim's boundary stated first, because the strongest objection comes from que-6's own formalism: D-optimality is invariant under nonsingular reparameterization, so if the joint coordinates were merely a nonsingular relabeling of what the bank already measures, and every cross-instrument map were already known, the within-bank D-optimal spine WOULD be the joint one. The bend is real exactly where InSight's case breaks those conditions: other axioms measure dimensions the bank reaches weakly or not at all, and the cross-instrument maps are themselves still under estimation. Three arguments. (1) Intersection mass: adaptive tails fragment item-level answered populations by design, so the spine is the only part of the bank whose per-item n grows like the whole population; a questions×other-axiom coupling's n is the intersection of the axioms' populations (pat-4), and at item level the question-side membership of that intersection is essentially the spine — comparability inside the bank (que-1's original framing) is only half the spine's job. The channel stated precisely, per the adversarial pass: once an item is in the spine everyone answers it, so ADDING spine items does not raise any coupling's n. Intersection mass is delivered by spine membership; size enters at (3) through coverage, not through n. (2) Composition: the estimand decides the optimum, and the joint criterion splits the budget between two item roles. LINKING items content-overlap what another axiom measures and identify the cross-instrument map onto the shared space — a same-construct bridging estimand: coupling geometry between DISTINCT constructs needs only jointly measured people, which spine membership already supplies, but identifying how the bank's scale maps onto another instrument's requires items touching that instrument's construct. COMPLEMENTARY items add joint information conditional on what the other axioms already pin — an item duplicating what sensors measure well adds little; an item on a dimension no other axiom reaches adds much. The split is a continuum (the angle between an item's information direction and the already-measured subspace), not a partition. How the optimal split moves over the program's life is an explicit PREDICTION, not a derivation: pinning the maps should release linking budget toward complementarity, but each newly priced coupling or newly added axiom renews linking demand — which pressure dominates is an empirical question, and the split's trajectory would itself be a measurable signal of the combination's maturity. (3) Size: the portfolio floors spine size through dimension coverage. Each priced coupling names question-side dimensions that must be measured to a target reliability for everyone in the intersection ('target reliability' is this node's construct, layered on pat-4's budget-and-marginal-value frame — pat-4 does not itself assign per-coupling precision targets); reliability per dimension requires a minimum item count, and the dimensions needing coverage multiply with axioms and priced pairs. So que-1's open problem gains an argument: spine size is f(population, bank size, coupling portfolio), the portfolio entering through which dimensions must be covered and how well. Two inherited fragilities, named: cen-1 is argued and flags its own fork (if audit-layer faithfulness cannot be measured, the published joint coordinate system degrades from specification to aspiration) — this node's composition argument inherits that fork. And an open tension with que-6 stands deliberately: que-6's anchor logic wants the spine to span what the BANK measures, this node wants composition set on the JOINT space; under a fixed answer budget those compete for the same slots, and neither node yet prices the trade — the most valuable open problem this run surfaced. Status held at argued deliberately: the equating and optimal-design scaffolding is cited at que-6, but the cross-axiom bending itself is this lane's own argument — no external source claims it, and §4 says the status stays down.

nodes.claim: The shared spine plays the anchor set's linking role from equating theory — and the mini-version prescription is partly relaxable: with content coverage and mean difficulty held, a narrower difficulty spread equates about as well.
nodes.detail: Added 2026-08-27 as the grounded scaffolding under que-5; claim narrowed by the adversarial pass before landing to exactly what the cited evidence tested. The spine's linking role is the same structure as the common-item nonequivalent-groups design — classical two-form NEAT is the special case; InSight's spine-plus-adaptive-tail is item-pool linking as in CAT calibration — where the common items are what make measurements from people who otherwise answered different item sets comparable. The field's standard prescription, that the anchor be a miniature of the full instrument in content and statistical specifications, is documented at first hand in Sinharay & Holland's own abstract (their study 'questioned conventional wisdom that an anchor test should be a statistical miniature version of the tests being equated'); Kolen & Brennan stands in the source list as the standard text of the field, with no specific page-level content claim hung on it — it was not readable at first hand from this container. What Sinharay & Holland actually tested and found: holding content coverage representative and mean item difficulty equal, anchors with a NARROWER spread of item difficulty equated about as well as mini-version anchors — so the spread half of statistical mimicry is relaxable, and their result licenses nothing about relaxing content coverage or mean difficulty; this node deliberately claims nothing beyond it. For InSight: the spine should cover the content of what needs linking — per que-5, that is bent toward the joint space, and the que-5↔que-6 budget tension (span the bank vs identify the joint space under one fixed budget) is the open problem both nodes now name. The selection formalism que-1 and que-5 lean on is likewise standard: item choice as maximization of information about the estimand (van der Linden 1998 for the Bayesian criterion; van der Linden 2005 for test assembly as constrained optimization), and Berger–King–Wong for the D-optimality frame together with its standard robustification — information-optimal designs are locally optimal, i.e. optimal against current parameter estimates (que-2's calibration-drift warning in design form), and minimax design is the paper's remedy for exactly that.
